answer_1.quote: this paper focuses on the task of citing sentence generation

answer_2.quote: Following previous work, we report ROUGE-1 (unigram), ROUGE-2 (bigram), and ROUGE-L (longest common subsequence) scores to evaluate the generated citing sentences.

answer_4.quote: We sampled 50 instances from the generated texts. Three graduate students who are fluent in English and familiar with NLP were asked to rate citing sentences produced by BACO and the re-implemented PTGEN-Cross with respect to four aspects on a 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) point scale: fluency (whether a citing sentence is fluent), relevance (whether a citing sentence is relevant to the cited paper's abstract), coherence (whether a citing sentence is coherent within its context), and overall quality.
answer_4.guideline: rate citing sentences with respect to four aspects: fluency, relevance, coherence, and overall quality
